findings.summary: The header-injection check (assertValidHeaderValue) was removed and normalizeValue now silently strips CR/LF/control characters instead of rejecting them, so injection attempts go unnoticed and merged values can change meaning (e.g. pass allowlist checks).
The regex [^\x09\x20-\x7E\x80-\xFF] silently drops \x7F and all code points above 0xFF (e.g. € or CJK), corrupting header values without error, and tests don't cover it.
trimSPorHTAB now trims leading and trailing whitespace on every header value, a behavior change for all callers beyond the injection case.
Loopback aliasing means no_proxy=localhost now also bypasses the proxy for 127.0.0.1 and [::1] and vice versa, which is wider than what the user typed (deliberate but worth noting).
Updated tests only assert the new sanitizing behavior and do not check that header injection is detected or rejected.
